exercise.name: RKC Plank
steps: Get into a forearm plank with elbows slightly ahead of your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes, thighs and fists as hard as you can.
Pull your elbows toward your toes without moving, and hold.
exercise.one_line_summary: A hold (one picture): forearm plank on the toes with the elbows close together (~0.15 m) and placed forward of the shoulders (upper arm ~10 deg past vertical, elbow ~100 deg), fists thumb-up, feet together, glutes squeezed into a posterior pelvic tilt, body one straight rigid line. Rectus abdominis is the target; obliques and glutes clearly work.

setup.target: Elbows about 6 in (0.15 m) apart, forward toward the head so the elbow angle is ~100 deg.
setup.tolerance: elbow gap 0.10-0.20 m; elbow 95-110 deg interior
setup.why: NSCA technique column (S2): elbows ~6 in apart at nose level, ~100 deg; the longer lever is what raises EMG (S1).

setup.target: Fists, thumbs up, little fingers on the floor.
Glutes squeezed hard: pubic bone toward the belly button, tailbone toward the feet (posterior tilt).
setup.tolerance: pelvis tipped 3-8 deg posterior vs neutral

movement.measure: torso slope; rot X 90 = flat face-down
movement.start: ~85.7 effective (shoulders 4.3 deg higher than the ankles)

movement.measure: pelvis rot X vs the torso line
movement.start: -5 deg (root 80.7 with spine05 +3, spine04 +2 bringing the trunk back to the line)
96.5 / 123 (elbow ahead of and inside the shoulder)

muscles.emg: Long-lever posterior-tilt plank > traditional plank for upper RA (p<0.001) and lower abdominal stabilisers (p<0.001) (S1). Plank with scapular adduction and posterior pelvic tilt: RA ~78% MVIC (Cortell-Tormo, in S3).
muscles.role: Resists the trunk sagging under the longer lever; what the exercise is for.
muscles.surface: Vertical bands down the front of the belly.

muscles.emg: EO higher than traditional plank (p<0.001) (S1); posterior-tilt plank: EO 110.8 +- 65.8% and IO 119.9 +- 60.3% MVIC (Cortell-Tormo, in S3).
muscles.role: Brace the trunk; the posterior tilt raises them most. EMG equals or beats RA, but the exercise's named purpose (abs) keeps the primary slot.

muscles.emg: Not measured in S1; contracted 'as strongly as possible' by design (S2).
muscles.role: Hold the posterior pelvic tilt and the hips extended.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Belly sinks below the shoulder-ankle line.
mistakes.why_it_matters: S2: the body must stay rigid; called the common error.
Removes the long lever that makes this variation harder (S1).

sources.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Contreras B, Tiryaki-Sonmez G, Willardson JM, Fontana F. 2014. An electromyographic comparison of a modified version of the plank with a long lever and posterior tilt versus the traditional plank exercise. Sports Biomech 13(3):296-306. doi:10.1080/14763141.2014.942355
sources.what_it_gave: LLPTP > traditional for upper RA, lower abdominals, EO; long lever contributes more than the tilt; tilt alone raises EO.

sources.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Contreras BM. 2013. Exercise technique: the long-lever posterior-tilt plank. Strength Cond J (NSCA).
sources.what_it_gave: Feet together, fists thumbs up, elbows ~6 in apart at nose level, elbow ~100 deg, straight line, glutes max, pubic bone up / tailbone down; 2-3 x 10-30 s.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Front plank with scapular adduction + posterior pelvic tilt (Cortell-Tormo): IO 119.9%, EO 110.8%, RA ~78% MVIC.

clip_check.check: Elbows ahead of and closer than the shoulders
clip_check.target: elbow gap 0.10-0.20 m; elbow 0.03-0.08 m toward the head from under the shoulder

clip_check.check: Toes on the floor, feet together
clip_check.target: lowest foot point -0.002..+0.002 m; ankle gap < 0.15 m
hip within 0.03 m of the shoulder-ankle line
abs strongest red; obliques and glutes light
